newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia would be happy to see Thais take Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia would be happy to see Thais take Pol Pot.

text.p: Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Tuesday he would welcome any offer of refuge by neighbouring Thailand to notorious Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot and his henchmen.

Ranariddh said he could not confirm a Phnom Penh newspaper report on Tuesday which quoted an army commander as saying a deal had been reached with hardline Khmer Rouge leaders allowing them exile in exchange for the surrender of their troops.
"I haven't got any information about that," Ranariddh told reporters when asked about the report, which did not mention Thailand by name.
"But if Thailand feels pity, and lets Pol Pot, Son Sen and Ta Mok stay in Thailand I would welcome that in order to solve the remaining problems."
Son Sen is the guerrilla group's defence chief and Ta Mok is the rebels' powerful northern zone commander.
A senior security official in Ranariddh's party said the Khmer Rouge issue would be resolved this month.
"Everything will be cleared up this month. Pol Pot, Ta Mok and Son Sen have a good place to live," Serei Kosal told reporters. He declined to say where the trio might live.
A Thai embassy official in Phnom Penh said he doubted Bangkok would ever offer refuge to the Khmer Rouge leaders.
"It would be very unlikely. We consider the Khmer Rouge an internal affair of Cambodia. Our policy is they have to solve this problem themselves," the embassy official told Reuters.
A senior Thai offical in Bangkok involved in policy towards Cambodia said it would be "impossible" for Thailand to take the three Khmer Rouge leaders.
"I think China is the most suitable country for them if they were to be exiled," he said.

The Cambodia Daily newspaper published a report citing General Nhiek Bun Chhay as saying Pol Pot, Son Sen and Ta Mok had agreed to abandon their jungle strongholds and go into exile while allowing their troops to defect to the government.
He did not say where the three guerrilla leaders might live but said nominal Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan would be allowed to enter Cambodian politics.
Nhiek Bun Chhay was not available for comment on Tuesday and other defence officals could not confirm the report.
An intelligence source in Thailand said there had been some negotiations between the Cambodian government and the Khmer Rouge but he was not aware of any exile arrangement.

The Thai source suggested Nhiek Bun Chhay, who is a senior member of Ranariddh's party, might be testing the waters with his announcement of a deal to see what the reaction might be in Phnom Penh where the guerrillas have become a factor in a long-running feud between Ranariddh and his co-premier Hun Sen.

The Khmer Rouge split last year with a more moderate faction based in the northwest of the country defecting to the government while the hardliners under Pol Pot remained in their jungle bases in Cambodia's far north.
The moderate faction has said it will remain politically neutral for now and would support the rightful winners of an election due next year.
Hardline faction member Khieu Samphan said in a recent guerrilla radio broadcast he would support an alliance formed by Ranariddh.

The Khmer Rouge, responsible for the deaths of more than one million people during their 1975-1979 rule, signed a peace treaty in 1991 officially ending the Cambodian war but refused to take part in the subsequent peace process or U.N-run polls in 1993.
